note: Root of every script class (no superclass). Monitor methods work on ANY object, scripts use them as condition variables (see Thread notes).

Blocks the calling script thread until another thread calls notify/notifyAll on the SAME object. Pattern: `while(1){ obj.wait(); ... }` (GameLogic.run waits on `timeRefresher`, GameType.run waits on `mp`, LoadingScreen.run waits on `Frontend.render`). No timeout form exists. There is no matching lock/unlock: scripts never use `synchronized` (the in-engine compiler rejects it); mutual exclusion comes from the cooperative scheduler.

Cooperative script thread. The VM runs threads in time slices (Thread::run(float budget), docs/research/script-vm-opcodes.md), there is no preemption inside a slice and no exceptions. A Thread is a java.lang.Native: `ptr` holds the engine thread object.

protected native called by the constructor `Thread(Runnable target, String name)` with the NAME only; the target is stored in the script field `target`. Order inside the constructor: `super(); init(name); this.target = target`. `Thread()` and `Thread(String)` use `this` as target.

Schedules the thread to run `target.run()`. The target may be a STATIC `run()` method (GameLogic declares `static void run()` and passes `this`), so the engine's lookup of `run` must accept static methods.
Kills the thread (no unwinding, no finally). Used for `timeRefresher.stop()` in GameLogic.finalize, GameType.leaveAsyncMode_Script_Real, Mechanic/CarLot worker threads.

Pure script class (no natives). `set(v)` stores `value` and notifyAll(); `waitFor(v)` loops `while(value != v) wait()`. Both methods have flags 0x81 (public + 0x80; 0x80 is probably 'synchronized/atomic' in TUFA, never used by the compiler for anything else in the corpus).

Strings are VM objects (`java.lang.Native` subclass). `+` concatenates and formats int/float operands (operator 0x10, `unsupported type (+)` otherwise). The float-to-text format of `+` is NOT known (open question 4); `Float.toString(f, fmt)` is the explicit formatter.

Base of every scripted game object (Part, Vehicle, Osd, GameLogic, Init, Config, Controller...). Extends GameRef, so a GameType IS a handle to its own world-tree node. The engine instantiates subclasses; see entry-points.md for how and for the callbacks the engine invokes (handleEvent, handleEventAsync, control, drive, animate, getInfo, finalize).

Subscriber API: `subscriber.addNotification(GameRef source, int eventMask, int deliverAs, String filter [, String handlerName])`. When `source` raises an event in eventMask, the engine calls `handlerName(GameRef source, int event, String params)` on the subscriber (default name `handleEvent`). deliverAs is always GameRef.EVENT_SAME (0), filter is always null in the corpus. Handler names seen: "event_handlerRocFence", "event_handlerRaceFinish", "event_handlerClick", "event_handler"+suffix (Osd.addHook, used for EVENT_CURSOR).
Undoes addNotification(source, mask).

`addTimer(float seconds, int id)`: ONE-SHOT timer. After `seconds` the engine calls `handleEvent(GameRef self, EVENT_TIME, id)` (int overload). GameLogic re-arms itself every time: `addTimer(timeRefreshRate, 0)` inside the handler. Values seen: seconds 1,5,3,10,2; ids 2,4,0,7,3.
Cancels pending timers of this object (called in finalize of Chassis and tracks).

Sets (replaces) the events THIS object accepts: EVENT_CURSOR x13, EVENT_TIME x7, EVENT_COLLISION, EVENT_COMMAND. Without EVENT_TIME in the mask addTimer events are not delivered (GameLogic calls setEventMask(EVENT_HOTKEY|EVENT_TIME)).
`clearEventMask(EVENT_ANY)` in finalize/destructors (19 of 22 sites).

`registerCallback(GII_CONTROL)` / `registerCallback(GII_ANIMATE)`: asks the engine to call the script's `control(float dt)` / `animate()` every tick. enableControlHook/enableAnimateHook wrap it. Other GII_* ids (GII_DRIVE=9) probably select `drive()`.
Counterpart of registerCallback.

Creates the engine-side (C++) twin of a script object that was made by `new` (not by GameRef.create). Handle to a node of the resource tree (the .rpk entries merged into one tree). `ResourceRef` is a Native: the constructor runs newNative() then set(id); finalize runs deleteNative(). Equality of refs is by id(); null/0 means 'no resource'.
Called by the constructor (`<init>() { super(); newNative(); }`). Allocates the C++ handle in `ptr`. Always paired with deleteNative() in finalize().
Called from finalize() (script GC). Releases the handle.
set(int id) / set(ResourceRef) rebinds the handle; `set(null)` or `set(0)` clears (release()). id is the global resource id; literals like `parts:0xAB5Cr` compile to constants of this id space.
Synchronous load of the resource (mesh/texture/sound) or, on a save-game string, (by-name sites `Vehicle.load(path,...)`, `GameLogic.load` are unrelated script statics).
Releases the resource data (CarMarket/Garage unload the map ref on exit).
